title: Abdul El-Sayed Mocks Trump and Ted Cruz’s Cruel Rhetoric on ‘The View,’ Jokes He Wants ‘Jihadist Leprechaun’ Printed on a Hat

The 42-year-old Democrat, who defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate , reflected on the Islamophobic rhetoric that dominated the final weeks of his campaign and credited Michigan voters with rejecting the divisive attacks. I took a bet on the goodness of the people of Michigan.” During the interview, Sunny Hostin ran through some of the most incendiary remarks made about El-Sayed by prominent Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, who suggested there was something “very, very evil” about him, and Sen. title: Robert Pattinson To Receive 40th Annual American Cinematheque Award

It just got better. Pattison will be the recipient of the 40th American Cinematheque Award, a milestone celebration taking place February 9, 2027 at the Beverly Hilton. Related Stories Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Tonys, Guilds & More Below The Line Hollywood Music In Media Awards Nominations: ‘Michael,’ ‘The Odyssey’ & More With a career spanning more than two decades, Pattinson has established himself as one of the most distinctive actors of his generation, moving seamlessly between independent cinema and major studio productions. In 2026, Pattinson’s versatility was showcased when he starred in no less than four films, all so vastly different from one another that the only commonality between them was him. From a happily engaged turned spiraling groom opposite Zendaya in A24’s darkly funny The Drama to the playfully villainous Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster The Odyssey to his critically acclaimed portrayal of journalist Chris Hansen in the psychological thriller, Primetime to a shapeshifting ‘Face Dancer’ assassin in the upcoming Dune: Part Three , Pattinson’s range has been on full display. Pattinson is currently in production on Matt Reeves’s The Batman Part II , the sequel to 2022’s highly successful The Batman . Watch on Deadline PRIMETIME, Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, 2026. © A24 / Courtesy Everett Collection American Cinematheque Board Chair Rick Nicita announced the selection by stating, “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices, and remarkable versatility as an actor. From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling. Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry. We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” In 2025, Pattinson starred in and executive produced Die, My Love , alongside Jennifer Lawrence. Additionally, Pattinson starred in Bong Joon Ho’s Mickey 17 , with Steven Yeun, Naomi Ackie and Toni Collette. Other notable credits include Christopher Nolan’s Tenet , Robert Eggers’ The Lighthouse , opposite Willem Dafoe, and Josh and Benny Safdie’s Good Time . Robert Pattinson is Antinous in ‘The Odyssey’ Universal Pattinson gained industry attention at 19 years of age when he joined the Harry Potter franchise in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and is also known worldwide for The Twilight Saga . For four decades, the prestigious American Cinematheque Award has been designed to recognize extraordinary artists whose talent, vision, and contributions have made a lasting impact on cinema. Their passion and filmography not only exemplify excellence in filmmaking but also reflect the cinematic artistry and breadth of American Cinematheque’s programming, which bridges film history to its future and celebrates the theatrical experience. The award has celebrated an impressive roster of filmmakers and performers, including among others Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman, George Clooney, and last year Michael B. Jordan who received the honor before going on to win the Best Actor Academy Award. The 40th Annual American Cinematheque Award Gala will be executive produced by Rick Nicita of RPMedia, along with Madelyn Hammond and Javier Infante of Hammond Infante Productions. It serves as an annual fundraiser for the non-profit organization, supporting its year-round programming at the Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz, and Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood. title: Emmy Rossum Named RAINN Ambassador Amid New Partnership to Deepen Public Understanding of Sexual Violence and Survivorship (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abbey White Plus Icon Abbey White Contributing Writer View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emmy Rossum Lelanie Foster Emmy Rossum has been named an ambassador for RAINN, the country’s largest anti-sexual violence organization, as the actress and nonprofit launch a new partnership focused on deepening the public’s understanding of sexual violence and survivorship. The Furious star will unite her platform as an artist and storyteller with the nonprofit’s expertise in survivor support to explore how storytelling can inform the public around the realities and misconceptions about sexual trauma and healing. The partnership aims to challenge stigma, amplify survivor voices, use storytelling to connect survivors with critical resources and encourage more thoughtful representations of sexual violence across the entertainment industry. Related Stories TV Newport Beach Film Fest: 'Furious' Star Emmy Rossum Will Receive TV Performance Award, Guest on Live Episode of 'Awards Chatter' Pod TV Why Emmy Rossum Says 'Shameless' Nude Scenes Affected Her Dating Life: "All These Preconceived Notions" “Working on Furious alongside psychologists and survivors reminded me that there is no perfect way to be a survivor,” Rossum says. “I’ve been so moved by the conversations the show has started. As we’ve seen too often of late, survivors are everywhere — from the halls of Congress to college campuses to the film industry — and this conversation belongs to all of us. Through my partnership with RAINN, I hope to turn that awareness into action: opening up conversations, breaking down stigma and helping more survivors find pathways to connection, support and healing.” The collaboration extends the connection to these issues that Rossum, among the nation’s more than 78 million survivors of sexual violence, developed while preparing for her critically acclaimed performance in Hulu’s Furious as Alice Black, an FBI agent and abuse survivor. While making the Elizabeth Meriwether-created series, production leaned on a community of consultants, including numerous survivors of sex trafficking, intimate partner violence experts, forensic psychologists, trauma therapists, FBI agents and human trafficking task force members. RAINN also served as a script consultant on the studio side during the show’s early development. “To tell these stories without re-traumatizing viewers, without explicitly showing the trauma, but instead, as Liz so cleverly did, showing the aftermath of the trauma, takes a lot of care,” the actress says. “What I’m most proud of in our show is how we demonstrated that survivors need not be innocent or likable to deserve dignity or justice. I think understanding the nuances of these crimes, understanding the struggles of survivors and how imperfect people still deserve the right to justice is important.” The announcement comes one day before Rossum will appear at Raising the Prevention Generation, an invite-only event for survivors, allies and advocates, co-hosted by WME and RAINN. The intimate brunch and sitdown in L.A. will feature Rossum; RAINN founder and president Scott Berkowitz; Jennifer Simmons Kaleba, RAINN vp, communications; Aspire Titan Academy student mental health therapist Skye Choe; and Dr. Karen Kay Imagawa, medical director of the Audrey Hepburn CARES Center at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles. The discussion will span how the adults in children’s lives can talk about sexual violence, consent and boundaries in a digital world and how everyone can turn current conversations into meaningful action. “One of the most meaningful parts of our work at WME is helping our clients turn what they care deeply about into real impact. Storytelling has an incredible power to change hearts, minds and perspectives, and Emmy’s commitment to using her voice with such care and purpose is a beautiful example of that,” says Jeanell English, head of community and impact at WME. “Together with RAINN’s decades of expertise, this partnership creates an opportunity to spark important conversations, challenge stigma and make a meaningful difference in how survivors are seen, heard and supported.” Friday’s talk will mark the first step in Rossum and RAINN’s newly minted alliance, which sprung out of a connection made during WME’s inaugural Women’s Health Summit, held in Los Angeles on Oct. 15. Rossum and RAINN chief of victim services Megan Cutter’s intimate fireside conversation “Furious? Good. Now What?” explored the ongoing myths and stereotypes that shape how sexual violence is perceived, the ways survivors respond to trauma and why survivor agency matters. “In recent weeks, calls to RAINN’s National Sexual Assault Hotline increased 73 percent,” Cutter says. “The country is having a hard and necessary conversation about sexual violence right now. Too often, what’s missing is an understanding of what survivors actually go through: that trauma responses vary, that there is no single right way to react and that healing looks different for everyone. Emmy and WME were committed to telling these stories with integrity long before this moment, and that’s what makes them the right partners to help carry this conversation forward.” The collaboration is particularly timely, arriving amid a moment flooded with national headlines and public discussions about sexual assault in the film and TV industry, on college campuses like Cornell University and the University of Chicago, as well as the campaign trail, in states like Maine, Ohio and Arizona. “ Cornell isn’t an outlier . It’s a reflection of what happens on campuses and in communities every day. The difference is that people are paying attention right now,” says Berkowitz. “[It] landed hard because it felt so real. The details differ, but for the tens of millions of Americans who’ve experienced sexual violence, this story was personal and for a lot of parents, it was a wake-up call. Nobody wants their kid to be a victim — or a perpetrator.” The partnership also comes nearly a decade after the #MeToo movement changed public discourse around sexual violence and how survivors are treated. In the years since, the movement has faced backlash and shifts in attention and momentum, but alongside the recent news about campus assaults, Rossum explains why addressing sexual assault must go beyond a moment. “#MeToo was an incredibly important watershed moment in culture. But all social movements require sustained action,” says Rossum. “Sunlight remains the best disinfectant. What happened at Cornell needs to be brought into the light . When our leaders foster a culture that threatens the safety of women, it needs to be called out directly and swiftly.” According to the actress and producer, the most impactful way she and her fellow creative community members can do that is by tackling the issues through storytelling. “There is something about taking the shame out of things by putting them on screen for us to see, warts and all. A character can reach us emotionally in a way that a PSA can’t. We aren’t just being told about something. We’re feeling it alongside someone, and that can change how we understand and treat each other,” she tells The Hollywood Reporter . “That’s the power of stories to me: It can take something that feels isolating and create a connection around it.” That’s why stories are at the forefront of her upcoming work with RAINN. “They can make us feel seen and less alone. That connection matters long after the headlines go away,” says Rossum. “No one was asking for Furious or Josephine or I May Destroy You or even Obsession , which sparked important conversations about consent. But audiences turned out because they’re phenomenal stories about something important. We need to keep telling them.” For RAINN, partnering with a storyteller like Rossum means the conversation around sexual assault, trauma and survivorship does not only have to live within a news cycle and “can reach people who’ve never thought of sexual violence as their issue and help keep this conversation going long after the headlines fade,” says Berkowitz. “The stakes of not talking about this are high. When people don’t understand consent, harm happens. When friends don’t know what to look for, they don’t step in. And when survivors don’t recognize what happened to them, or the people they confide in respond with doubt or blame, healing gets much harder,” he continues. “Sexual assault isn’t an abstract statistic. It’s happening to people we know and love and talking about it openly is how we prevent it and how we support survivors.” THR

title: Chris Pratt Tapped for King of Comedy Award at 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Pratt CBS/Nickelodeon Chris Pratt has been tapped to receive the King of Comedy Award at the 2026 Kids’ Choice Awards on Nov. 14. The Guardians of the Galaxy and Parks and Recreation alum will receive the Silver Blimp statuette at the show, which is officially titled CBS Presents Nickelodeon Kids’ Choice Awards, in celebration of his career, “before facing Nickelodeon’s iconic slime,” according to the announcement. Pratt also might take home an Orange Blimp award that night as he is nominated for favorite male animated voice from a movie for his role as Mario in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. Related Stories TV Tony Awards to Air on CBS Through 2032 TV Alex Warren to Host Kids' Choice Awards, Airing on CBS for the First Time; Taylor Swift Leads Nominees Pratt next stars in Way of the Warrior Kid, an adaptation of Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel that premieres Nov. 25 on Apple TV, which he also produced. “I’m incredibly honored to receive Nickelodeon’s King of Comedy Award,” Pratt said. “I spent most of my childhood trying to make people laugh to get out of trouble. Now apparently you can win awards for it. Pretty sweet deal. Comedy has always been a huge part of my life, and making people laugh is one of my favorite things in the world. Especially kids. I’m grateful to Nickelodeon and CBS for this honor. And if I get slimed, just know I’ll be sending them my dry-cleaning bill.” The 2026 KCAs will be hosted by Alex Warren . Musical performances and other celebrity appearances will be announced at a later date. Taylor Swift leads this year’s nominees with a total of six mentions, followed by Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter with five apiece. Awards will be handed out across film, television, music, gaming, sports and other categories. Among the movies and series that are up for KCAs are The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Toy Story 5, Wednesday , Wicked: For Good , The SpongeBob Movie: Search for SquarePants, KPop Demon Hunters and Percy Jackson and the Olympians. In addition, producers this year have introduced three new categories: watch party: kids’ choice, favorite onscreen duo/trio and favorite clutch player of the year. The 2026 KCA ceremony will air on CBS for the first time as well as on Nickelodeon. It also will stream live on Paramount+ for Premium subscribers in the U.S., with on-demand viewing available the following day for Premium and Essential subscribers. The ceremony airs live from Television City in Los Angeles at 8-9:30 p.m. ET/5-6:30 p.m. PT. The KCAs are produced by Done + Dusted. THR

title: AFM Hot Project: Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon Join ‘I’m With Stupid’ (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon, Ego Nwodim, Chabely Ponce Jenna Berman, Alexandra Carillo-Vaccino, Oriana Layendecker Ego Nwodim and Chabely Ponce are set to star in I’m With Stupid , a high school comedy directed by Hannah Pearl Utt ( Cora Bora ). Upgrade is handling international sales on the project and will launch it to buyers at the upcoming American Film Market . Written by Carolina Barlow ( The Hawk ) and Peter Kelly ( Big Mouth ), the film follows a pair of directionless high school seniors from opposite ends of the social spectrum who are forced to work together to avoid the humiliation of failing senior year. Related Stories Movies Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet's 'Violette' for U.S. Movies Suzanne Farwell's Starry Rom-Com 'Otherwise Engaged' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM (Exclusive) Tremblay ( Room , Wonder , Good Boys ) plays Noah, a senior with an opinion on everything but no motivation. Ponce ( Girl Group ) is Hadley, Noah’s wealthy classmate who discovers she may have interests beyond becoming a trophy wife. McKinnon ( Barbie , Ghostbusters ) will portray Principal Dunlap, the school’s deeply unpopular and increasingly vindictive administrator. Nwodim ( Return to You , Hoppers ) is Ms. Reed, the students’ unconventional English teacher, who becomes an unlikely ally in their fight to graduate. “I’m thrilled to make a movie that’s this funny but has this much heart, with my dream group of collaborators,” Utt said. Mallory Schwartz ( The Morning Show, Cora Bora ) and Jen Goyne Blake ( Joyland ) are producing. Jonathan Kier and Matt Brodlie are executive producing for Upgrade, alongside Christine D’Souza for After Hours, Marc Danon and Kyle Fox for Fox Global Capital and April Shih for Diversity Hire. “There’s a real appetite for smart, unapologetically funny comedies,” said Kier and Brodlie of Upgrade. “Hannah has a terrific ability to find genuine emotion in absurd situations, and with this exceptional ensemble, we believe I’m With Stupid has all the ingredients to become a new generation’s favorite high school comedy.” Production on I’m With Stupid is set for February/March of 2027, with Rich Delia overseeing casting. UTA Film Finance Group and After Hours are co-representing the film for domestic sales. THR

title: Martin McDonagh to Receive Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Beatrice Verhoeven Plus Icon Beatrice Verhoeven Awards Editor bverhoeven Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Martin McDonagh Monica Schipper/Getty Images Wild Horse Nine writer and director Martin McDonagh will receive the Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award at the Palm Springs International Film Festival , the Palm Springs International Film Awards announced on Thursday. The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7 to Jan. 18. “Martin McDonagh remains one of our most distinctive and original voices in cinema today,” Festival Chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi says. “Over the course of his celebrated career, he has built a body of work that is humorous, timely and morally complex. Wild Horse Nine is another testament to his singular vision, and we are honored to recognize him and his extraordinary film with the Outstanding Achievement in Directing Award.” Related Stories Movies Milcho Manchevski's 'Sister Brother Manhole Cover' Wins Top Prize at Tokyo Film Fest TV Tony Awards to Air on CBS Through 2032 Wild Horse Nine stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as CIA agents who set out to Easter Island shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup to confront their dark pasts. Their trip gets turned upside down when they meet a pair of rebellious students, played by Mariana di Girolamo and Ailin Salas. McDonagh is an award-winning filmmaker and playwright whose credits include In Bruges , Seven Psychopaths , Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri and The Banshees of Inisherin . For Three Billboards and Banshees , he received Oscar nominations for best picture, best director for Banshees , and best original screenplay for In Bruges , Three Billboards and Banshees . title: How ‘Frontline’ Turned Into an Oscar-Winning Documentary Juggernaut
full_text: Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT How ‘Frontline’ Turned Into an Oscar-Winning Documentary Juggernaut Under Raney Aronson-Rath, the decades-old PBS doc series has started winning Oscars (“20 Days in Mariupol”) and appealing to younger generations online. By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest Judi Dench Tells All About Bond: It Was Daniel Craig’s Idea to ‘Have Me Killed’ 2 days ago Spike Lee Is Praying the Knicks Don’t Visit the Trump White House 3 days ago John Oliver Reviews ‘You Can See Everything’: Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans Are ‘Complete Lunatics’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source PBS/Frontline This year’s documentary Oscar race will pit a cringe comedy maestro against the most decorated documentary film producer of the past decade. While plenty of ink has been spilled over Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s form-shattering Elizabeth Holmes curio “You Can See Everything,” it would be a mistake to count out Raney Aronson-Rath. Aronson-Rath has been at the helm of “ Frontline ,” PBS ’ acclaimed investigative documentary series, since 2015. Under her watch, the program has won so many Emmys she’s lost count (it stands at 44) and launches around 20 documentaries a year. In 2024, it took home its first documentary Oscar for “20 Days in Mariupol,” a vivid and violent account of AP journalist Mstyslav Chernov and his colleagues’ time in the Ukrainian city as it withstood Russia’s invasion in early 2022. Related Stories 'Married at First Sight' U.K. Canceled by Channel 4 Following Sexual Assault Allegations Awkwafina's ‘Kate Might Die,’ ‘Outside of Cleveland’ With Alex Wolff Among Projects Selected for U.S. in Progress A few days after Chernov and his team escaped Mariupol with their footage, he and Aronson-Rath got to work on the film. “‘ 20 Days in Mariupol ’ was my debut film. [Raney] and the ‘Frontline’ team helped me practically and creatively transition from journalism to cinema, which is quite a challenge,” Chernov says, adding, “For many of us who are working on socially and politically relevant projects but cannot find a home and distributor, Raney is the last hope to get the film made and find its audience.” Oscar night was “a surreal moment” for Aronson-Rath. “People kept asking me, ‘Are you going to do more of these?!” she recalls. The common refrain was that “Frontline” couldn’t do theatrical films, and then one day it hit her: “I realized I was in charge of ‘Frontline,’ and we had the funding and distribution, so why not?” Aronson-Rath launched Frontline Features last November as a dedicated studio that premieres feature and short-form documentaries in festivals and theaters ahead of PBS airings. Its latest release is “One in a Million,” a feature doc from Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes that follows an 11-year-old girl, Israa, over 10 years as she and her family flee war-torn Syria to Turkey before settling in Germany. A powerful examination of war, immigration and the ties that bind, the film won the Audience Award at this year’s Sundance Film Festival and is poised to earn an Oscar nomination. “I was there from the very beginning. They sent me raw footage of Israa when she was 10 years old,” explains Aronson-Rath, a producer on the film. “I had a feeling that Israa’s story was going to be amazing.” On top of Aronson-Rath’s “extraordinary passion and professionalism,” Azzam is grateful that Frontline gave the project the benefit of time: “We were following real people going through major changes in their lives, which required patience, trust and a willingness to embrace uncertainty, and having that long-term commitment was essential,” explains Azzam. “Raney was always there with her unwavering belief in the film and her understanding that this wasn’t simply a story about refugees reaching Europe, but about what happens afterward: growing up in exile, searching for belonging and navigating identity.” Frontline also lent valuable “editorial experience,” Azzam maintains. Aronson-Rath’s team typically assigns investigative reporters to aid projects, conduct deep legal reviews and analyze rushes to make sure they meet their editorial standards. Aronson-Rath caught the journalism bug writing for The China Post, an English-language newspaper for expats in Taipei, after graduating from the University of Wisconsin. While attending the Columbia Journalism School, she caught a screening of Steve James’ 1994 documentary “Hoop Dreams” at Film Forum in downtown Manhattan. “It was a really transcendent moment for me,” she remembers. “I’d found the form that I love.” Years later, Aronson-Rath worked closely with James on “Abacus: Small Enough to Jail,” about a family-owned bank in Manhattan’s Chinatown that was the only financial institution to face criminal charges following the 2008 financial crisis; the doc earned “Frontline” its first Oscar nomination in 2018. “Public television has for decades tried to broaden its appeal to younger audiences, often without success,” says James. “From the day Raney took over, it was clear that she wanted to find more innovative ways to tell powerful true stories.” Frontline has, under Aronson-Rath, proven intensely popular among younger generations. Its YouTube channel has 4.8 million subscribers — eclipsing 1 billion views in July with an astonishing 422 million hours watched. It also has three features lined up for 2027, including Chernov’s next film, which Aronson-Rath will be producing. “One of the others is a film I’ve been working on for 20 years with a filmmaker named Dan Edge,” she shares, “focusing on one character we met two decades ago who came back from Iraq.” She flashes a grin. “I love a longitudinal, epic story.” ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Bloodaxe’: Season 2 of Amazon Viking Drama Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand, Lasse Steen to Cast ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon ‘Rose Hill’ Amazon Series Adds Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland Loading comments...

title: ‘Dune’ Launches Arrakis-Inspired Press-On Nail Collection With Glamnetic
full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. The world of “ Dune ” is getting the beauty treatment. Ahead of the Dec. 18 release of “Dune: Part Three,” Glamnetic has teamed up with Warner Bros. on a limited-edition collection of press-on nails inspired by the sci-fi franchise, marking its first foray into the beauty category. Launching Nov. 5, the limited-edition Glamnetic x Dune collection features nine nail sets drawing on the films’ characters, mythology and distinctive visual world, from the glowing blue eyes of the Fremen to the giant sandworms that roam Arrakis. The partnership marks the franchise’s first beauty collaboration, according to Glamnetic, with prices ranging from $21.99 to $23.99. Related Stories Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault in London Trial; Taken Into Custody ‘Bad Day’ Trailer: Cameron Diaz Is a Single Mom Who Accidentally Robs a Bank in Netflix Comedy Among the designs is “Spice Melange” ($21.99), featuring a translucent burnt-amber finish outlined in fine gold, inspired by the precious substance at the center of Frank Herbert’s fictional universe. “Eyes of Ibad” ($21.99) takes its cues from the Fremen’s signature blue-in-blue eyes, with iridescent cobalt chrome and an aurora-like shimmer. LIMITED-EDITION Dune x Glamnetic Collection shop now “The Maker” ($23.99) pays tribute to the franchise’s colossal sandworms through sculpted gold, amber and ridged chocolate-brown detailing, complete with a cobalt stone accent. “Reverend Mother” ($23.99) features a more elaborate combination of multicolored jewels, gold chrome, smoky mauve and black-and-gold detailing, while “Chip & Shatter” ($23.99) pairs a milky cream base with textured, crackled gold foil. The collection is the latest entertainment-inspired launch from Glamnetic, which has previously released licensed nail sets celebrating “Harry Potter,” including designs inspired by Hogwarts houses, the Marauder’s Map and the Deathly Hallows. The brand has also expanded into sports merchandise through a partnership with Fanatics, offering team-branded manicures featuring official NFL, NBA, MLB and other league logos and colors. The launch comes just over a month before “Dune: Part Three” arrives in theaters Dec. 18, bringing Villeneuve’s blockbuster trilogy to a close. The upcoming Warner Bros. and Legendary film draws from Herbert’s 1969 novel “Dune Messiah” and takes place nearly two decades after Paul Atreides’ rise to power, following the consequences of his reign as emperor and the growing threats to his rule. Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya return as Paul Atreides and Chani, alongside Florence Pugh, Anya Taylor-Joy, Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem and Jason Momoa. Robert Pattinson joins the franchise as Scytale, a central figure in the conspiracy against Paul. Villeneuve directs from a screenplay co-written with Brian K. Vaughan. The franchise has already proved fertile ground for unconventional merchandise partnerships. Ahead of 2024’s “Dune: Part Two,” watchmaker Hamilton collaborated with the filmmakers to create a futuristic wrist device worn in the film, subsequently releasing two limited-edition Ventura watches inspired by the prop. Chalamet also worked with Cartier on a custom necklace for the film’s London premiere, featuring roughly 900 gemstones in desert-inspired shades of amber, orange and blue. The Glamnetic collection offers a considerably more affordable entry point into the world of Arrakis, arriving just in time for the franchise’s theatrical finale and the holiday shopping season. full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT Robert Pattinson to Receive 40th American Cinematheque Award By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Pixar Names Jonathan Garson as President; Jim Morris Moves to Emeritus Role 16 hours ago Neve Campbell Confirms Return for ‘Scream 8’ 3 days ago ‘X-Men’: ‘Hunger Games’ Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel’s Reboot 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Stefanie Keenan Robert Pattinson will be honored as the 40th recipient of the American Cinematheque Award. Pattinson receives the award in celebration of his own two-decade career, in which he’s established himself as one of the most versatile actors of his generation. The actor will be feted on Feb. 9, 2027, at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills. “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices and remarkable versatility as an actor,” American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita stated, announcing Pattinson’s selection. “From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling.” Related Stories Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ Clio Barnard's 'I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning' Bought by Kino Lorber for North America (EXCLUSIVE) In 2026 alone, Pattinson starred opposite Zendaya in the dark romance “The Drama”; played the villainous Atinuous in Christopher Nolan’s epic “The Odyssey” and portrayed “To Catch a Predator” journalist Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” which also marked the debut film from Pattinson’s production company Icki Eneo Arlo. title: How Grimes’ Cameo in Theater-Bound AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Came Together (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT How Grimes’ Cameo in Theater-Bound AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Came Together (EXCLUSIVE) By Corbin Bolies Plus Icon Corbin Bolies Latest Scarlett Johansson Says ‘The Batman 2’ Role Was ‘Very Hard to Figure Out’: ‘It Gave Me a Lot of Existential Angst’ 19 hours ago Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses 3 days ago Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Leader Hans Ku as Chief Product Officer 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fable Even in the AI era, there’s still no better way to reach a favorite artist than by sliding into their DMs. Zack London, who directed the upcoming AI film “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” under his moniker Gossip Goblin, had long been a fan of Grimes , the moniker of 38-year-old experimental pop artist Claire Boucher. But he didn’t necessarily expect that love to be mutual, not until he noticed she had followed his X account and started engaging with his videos. Related Stories South International Series Festival Prizes: ’Blindspot Berlin,’ ‘The Oligarch and the Art Dealer’ Win Big 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Spins Up Massive Numbers for Sony's Quarterly Earnings Then in March, Boucher replied to clips shared on Gossip Goblin’s X account. London responded , offering her a role in a project of his. Sensing an opportunity, he then sent Grimes a direct message just expressing how much he loved her music. “We started chatting, and it was like, ‘Oh, we know a ton of the same people,’” he tells Variety last month over lunch in Chelsea, coming off several prerelease screenings of the AI film. “She was like, ‘I would love to do something with you.’ And then, it was basically, ‘Well, I wish I knew that earlier, but let’s find a way for you to be in this.’” The fruit of those DMs will bear next month in Boucher’s minuteslong cameo in “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the first AI feature set to debut in theaters. Boucher plays “Zaynith Alda” in one of the early sequences in the post-apocalyptic film, which aims to satirize humanity’s relationship with technology. Alda, a brash, demanding aristocrat who hails from the rich Halvorith family, seeks a “dreamspool” an illicit, induced experience in the world of “NiiroCradle” that lets people experience alternate realities. Boucher’s cameo — and that of YouTuber and Logan Paul pal Mike Majlak, who also makes a brief appearance — injects a dash of celebrity into the bold ambitions of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the R-rated sci-fi film trying to barrel its way past society’s aversion to AI films and into the best animated feature category at the Oscars. Fable, the AI studio behind the film, has leaned in, setting a Times Square marketing campaign featuring Boucher’s appearance. Fable The studio also hosted screenings targeting animation voting bloc members of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences across New York and Los Angeles ahead of its Dec. 4 debut, eager to try and assuage the Academy’s concerns about all things AI and urge them to consider the gory film among the likes of the critically acclaimed “Wildwood” and “Toy Story 5.” (Variety’s “Awards Circuit” does not list “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” among the Academy’s potential contenders.) “You only need to see Grimes’ brilliant performance in the film to understand how much things are about to change for animated movies,” Fable CEO Edward Saatchi said in a bullish statement. “We hope the Academy will recognize that a film that is seminal (the first AI film), wildly technically novel and (most importantly) good deserves a nomination.” Boucher declined an interview request. Her spokesperson, Mitchell Jackson, said in a statement that Boucher “appreciates indie artists using new tools to create independent art—especially in the age of big studio monopolies.” “She was particularly impressed that they had such a large team and were involving and compensating so many artists, voice actors, and musicians,” her spokesperson said. “She believes in supporting the right kind of culture around AI in cinema rather than acquiescing to the current model of having no standards.” The Zaynith Alda character was already written into the film’s nearly two-hour runtime, but Boucher’s appearance forced London and his co-writer Jacob Batchelor to adapt the role around her persona. That meant giving her the chance to help design the character, including a mechanical-looking mask that adorns Alda’s face, and nixing the British accent native to the rest of the film’s world. Once those were set, a multi-continent team of London in Stockholm, his editor and sound engineer in Romania, and Boucher and her producer in LA worked together to record her lines from her home. Is there a recording anywhere of Boucher attempting a British accent? “If there are, they’re on a hard drive somewhere,” London says. Boucher is also one of the highest-profile examples of a celebrity authorizing their likeness for an AI project, following examples such as UFC fighters in Higgsfield’s “Cully Hill Boys” and “The View” co-host Sunny Hostin licensing her image and novels to Fountain 0 to make AI adaptations — featuring her likeness — of her books. It’s a testament to celebrities’ slow embrace of AI in culture, including everything from Ben Affleck’s Netflix-owned InterPositive startup for AI tools to actors like Michael Caine licensing his voice to the AI audio firm ElevenLabs. Others, however, remain fearful that AI could exploit their likenesses without permission or compensation . It helps that Boucher has long championed AI. In 2023, she launched an AI software program called “Elf.Tech,” where fans could use her vocal likeness in their tracks so long as she received 50% of the master recording royalties, and in a 2024 PBS interview called AI an “opportunity” for artists that, with democratized access to professional tools, could see “actual talent, like, really rise to the top.” For this film, London says Boucher authorized her license for free and refused to be paid, a fact her spokesperson confirmed. “She said, ‘You guys are scrappy, just put that money towards the other actors [and] your film,’” London says, calling Boucher part of “a different class of artists that look at the big picture of what are you doing, what is the holistic statement surrounding, and not getting hung up on the process.” Watch a clip of Boucher’s appearance below: ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Reacher’ Renewed for Season 6 Ahead of Season 5 Premiere ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson Loading comments...

title: ‘The Bend In The River’ Trailer: In Robb Moss Oscar Contender, Friends Reunite For Possibly Final Journey Down The Colorado
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Meryl Streep On How Fellow Oscar Winner Introduced Her To ‘My Undesirable Friends’ Documentary: “I Was Just Absolutely Entranced’ Magnolia Pictures To Qualify ‘Just Look Up’ For Oscars; Documentary Examines Climate Activist (And Standup Comedian) Michael Greenberg Doc Talk Podcast: Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival’s Ken Jacobson On State Of Nonfiction Filmmaking, Competitive Oscar Race And More View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: One of the most acclaimed documentaries of the year – nearly 50 years in the making – arrives on Netflix December 4. The Bend in the River , the Oscar-contending film directed by Robb Moss , marks the culmination of a cinematic project that began in the late 1970s with Riverdogs , which documented a rafting trip that Moss took with his friends down the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon. Those friends were in their 20s at the time, carefree and often clothing-free as they enjoyed life with the vitality and insouciance of youth. Moss documented another rafting trip with those friends in 2003’s The Same River Twice , his chums then in middle age. The new film finds the group rafting again, as river currents and the progress of time draw them closer to old age. Related Stories News Matthew McConaughey In 'The Rivals Of Amziah King'; Green Day-Inspired Road Trip Comedy 'Nimrods' -- Specialty Preview Documentary In 'The Bend In The River,' Friends Head Down The Colorado Again On Cinematic Journey Stretching Back Over 45 Years - Doc Stories Watch the trailer for the film above. Third River Films “The film interweaves moments from the distant past with those of the recent present,” notes a release, “taking viewers back-and-forth through time and inviting personal reflections on the inexorable flow of aging and the unfinished project of living.” In addition to his work as a filmmaker, Moss has taught film at Harvard University for over 30 years. Among his former students: Lance Oppenheim ( You Can See Everything ), two-time Oscar nominee Joshua Oppenheimer, Oscar nominees Yance Ford, RaMell Ross, and multiple Emmy nominee and Sundance Film Festival award winner Lauren Greenfield. Some extraordinary collaborators worked with Moss on The Bend in the River, including producers Lisa Remington (Oscar winner for The Only Girl in the Orchestra ) and Kristin Feeley, director of the Sundance Institute’s Documentary Film and Artist Programs. The film’s executive producers include Oscar winners Frances McDormand and Joel Coen as well as Oscar-winning producers Shane Boris ( Navalny ) and Jeff Reichert ( American Factory ). Moss received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Woods Hole Film Festival in Massachusetts. The Bend in the River earned the Artistic Vision Award at the Big Sky Documentary Film Festival in Montana and it won two awards at DOC LA, including Best Documentary and Best Editing, the latter award recognizing the work of Jeff Malmberg. It is set to screen at DOC NYC on November 12 after making that festival’s shortlist of the year’s best feature documentaries (DOC NYC calls it “a masterful meditation on the eternal, the temporal and the inevitable.”). Barry Wasserman stands behind an image of his younger self in ‘The Bend in the River’ Third River Films The Bend in the River screened at the 2025 edition of Doc Stories in San Francisco. At a Q&A there, Moss spoke about his approach to the filmmaking. “It’s not really built out of biography, ‘This happened and that happened,’” Moss said. “People had extraordinary lives, biographically, that aren’t in the film. And it seemed when there were scenes like that that had too much biography, it’s like the film flattened. But the whole thing had to move more… the dynamic of something going downstream. It just had to keep bouncing forward even as it went backwards and forwards. The beginning of the piece had to be very clear what we were up to, that there were going to be multiple timeframes. [But] there’s no saying there’s multiple films, there’s no saying there’s multiple timeframes, there’s no dates, timestamps, there’s no voiceover, there’s no music to cover up cuts.” Watch the trailer for The Bend in the River above. The company’s talent roster includes PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, RDCWorld, with brand clients that include Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova. ISO says it has more than 90 clients, with a heavy focus on livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers and lifestyle creators across beauty, food and other verticals. Creators are increasingly leveraging the audiences they have built through their streams and social channels to build businesses elsewhere, and at the same time brands are eager to work with creators on campaigns and original content. Firms like ISO can help connect those dots. “The next household name is already online, building an audience, and ISO was built for that talent,” said Mike Lee, CEO and co-founder of ISO. “Today’s gatekeepers are algorithms, so understanding discovery, engagement and how content travels is essential. Every creator we work with is running a real business, and our job is to give it room to grow through original IP, products, live events, and expansion into China and platforms like TikTok Shop, where most of the industry still isn’t set up to compete.” “At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment,” added Lylette Pizarro, founder & co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated. ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.” “Talent development used to be the heart of every company in the representation business. ISO is bringing it back with our model built for the new generation where musicians and creators increasingly share the same playbook: build an audience directly, then build a business around it,” said Darren Yan, co-founder and head of music at ISO. “We invest in our clients from the earliest stages across music, media, products, live events, gaming and tech, with our A&R team applying the same lens to artists by building global fandom online before the market catches on.” THR

full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:30am PT Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) 32 minutes ago Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ 2 hours ago ‘Rings of Power’ Star Eddie Marsan on Playing a Power-Hungry Dwarf and Why He Once Had 2,000 Pairs of Orlando Bloom’s Elf Ears in His Attic 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ashley Randall Wunmi Mosaku , the Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning star of Ryan Coogler’s 2025 hit “Sinners,” has come aboard British documentary short “Swim Sistas” as executive producer. The film, celebrating Black women’s relationship with swimming, was directed by Catherine Joy White (“Bridgerton,” “Fifty-Four Days”), with Naomie Harris (“Moonlight”) narrating. After premiering at DOC NYC and winning several awards on the festival circuit, it has now qualified for the 99th Academy Awards. Related Stories Sky News Stands by Journalist Following Heated Exchange With Abdul El-Sayed: 'We're Proud of Our Correspondent, Who Was Doing His Job' Lady Gaga, Jack White, Boy George Lead Songwriters Hall of Fame 2027 Nominees “The story of our relationship with swimming and water has so much depth and history, complexity that is so beautifully captured by ‘Swim Sistas,'” said Mosaku. “This powerful film and its themes speak personally to me, as I know it does many others, and I could not be more excited to join as executive producer. I believe ‘Swim Sistas’ will not only move people, but change how they see the world, and I’m proud to help its message reach a wider audience, and support its next chapter.” Featuring four Black British women, “Swim Sista” follows Alice Dearing, Great Britain’s first Black female Olympic swimmer; professional rugby player and “The Traitors” contestant Jasmine Boatswain; teenage athlete Lexie Sandiford; and Roni Bruno, who learned to swim at the age of 54. Through their stories, the documentary explores what it says are the “barriers, histories and joy that shape Black women’s relationships with water.” Featuring original poetry written by White, the film sees Harris voice Mami Wata, a central poetic figure embodying “ancestral strength and hope for the future.” “Wunmi is a stunning talent. Her work carries such depth and humanity and to have her join forces with ‘Swim Sistas’ brings another dimension to a world that has always been about so much more than swimming,” said White. “We’re honoured to have Wunmi on this journey with us as we continue to elevate Black women’s voices and reshape the story of who water is for.” Added Afua Hirsch and Amandla Crichlow, executive producers and founders of Born in Me Productions: “Wunmi Mosaku is an actor of such skill and grace, who represents the beauty and power of Black women in a way that has truly universal resonance. We could not be more proud to have her as a partner on ‘Swim Sistas.’” The attachment of Mosaku — also a BAFTA TV award winner for “Damilola, Our Loved Boy” — comes as the filmmakers behind “Swim Sistas” develop plans to expand the project into a documentary series exploring Black women’s relationships with water across the U.S., the Caribbean and Africa. Also joining the film’s executive producing team alongside Mosaku is BAFTA-nominated executive producer Ash Horne (“Marion,” “The Second Time Around”). “Growing up, swimming was something I always took for granted. It was simply part of being a kid and I never really questioned that privilege. So, when I learned that 97% of Black adults and around 80% of Black children in England don’t swim regularly, it really struck me,” said Horne. “‘Swim Sistas’ is a beautiful, heartfelt and important documentary that shines a light on this disparity while celebrating community and the joy of swimming. Catherine Joy White has created something genuinely moving, and I’m incredibly proud to support the film and help bring this conversation to a wider audience.” Originally announced in Variety , “Swim Sistas” has since screened at more than 50 festivals worldwide. Its accolades include best documentary at Women X, a BAFTA- and BIFA-qualifying festival, and the jury’s choice award at the Thomas Edison Film Festival, an Oscar-qualifying festival. The film has also enjoyed a 26-cinema theatrical run, screened at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., and opened special screenings of “The Little Mermaid” and “The Shape of Water.” It was featured at the inaugural United Nations Swimmable Cities Summit in Rotterdam and is being incorporated into the French national curriculum. “Swim Sistas” is produced by Oriane Pick and Anaïs Ferrato of BAFTA-nominated Candid Broads Productions, with executive producers Hirsch (“Enslaved,” “Africa Rising”) and Crichlow (“Honk for Jesus. title: Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music
full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:09am PT Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music Former UTA and FaZe Clan leaders aim to shape representation for digital-native stars By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music 38 minutes ago UFC’s Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings 19 hours ago Jessica Alba Battled ‘Major Impostor Syndrome’ as She Built The Honest Company Into an Early Star-Led Business Success Story 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tyler Ash Gaming and digital media veterans Mike Lee and Darren Yan have joined together to launch ISO , a talent management firm that specializes in representing the hottest commodities in marketing and media these days: creators and livestreaming personalities. Based in Los Angeles, Lee and Yan have quietly been building ISO’s operations for about a year, with financial backing from Influence Media Partners, an investment banner that also focuses on digital-native content. The launch of the firm draws on Lee and Yan’s breadth of experience working across gaming, sponsorship and branding and artist development. The pair have also built extensive partnership and distribution connections for entertainment and media platforms across Asia including in China. Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Lee, who was most recently head of gaming and livestreaming for UTA’s creators division, serves as co-founder and CEO of ISO. Yan, former chief talent officer at esports lifestyle firm FaZe Clan, serves as co-founder and head of music. ISO (which stands for In Search Of) at present has about 24 employees spread between Los Angeles, New York and Atlanta. The roster includes more than 90 livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers (aka livestreamers who use animated avatars) and lifestyle creators active in beauty, food and other highly engaged content verticals. Matt Alsberg, an alum of Sony’s PlayStation, Twitch and UTA, has signed on as ISO’s head of talent. “What we’re trying to build is something that is dedicated to the digital creator,” Lee tells Variety. Both founders have experience working at UTA and large-scale firms that are harnessing the heat of the next-generation stars of the attention economy. ISO was born out of Lee and Yan’s belief that talent representation firms have to operate very differently to support digital-native talent than they have for the past century in traditional film, TV and music. ISO’s roster at launch includes about 90 clients, including notable digital stars such as PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, jessechrisss, Angelo Marasigan, RDCWorld and more. ISO and its clients are alredy doing business with top-tier brands Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova, the ice cream brand known for its out-there shapes and flavors such as fried chicken. “If we really believe the next household name is going to come from the internet, then why aren’t all of our services optimized toward that internet star? We kept thinking, what if we were to actually blow everything up and we didn’t have an office and we weren’t spending millions of dollars on rent and theaters and showcases? Because our clients aren’t asking us for that,” Lee says. “There are no gatekeepers when it comes to digital media. It’s not four networks. It’s not seven channels. The gatekeepers are just the algorithms that feed your timelines. That’s what’s so incredible about working in this space.” Yan adds the pair’s proximity to explosive youth culture across Asia and in China, which has been an elusive market for so many U.S. firms, is a huge benefit to strategizing on where media and Gen Z and Gen Alpha consumption habits are headed. And it’s crucial for effective talent representation of digital dynamos. “For this generation, how they think and how they behave are not things are conditioned like a TV film actor or a sports athlete or even a music artist where they had to follow this specific pathway to success,” Yan tells Variety . “All of our clients are like, ‘Hey, we’re gonna break some eggs the way that we’re going to do it, and if you guys want to ride with us then you’re going to ride with us.’ That’s always been what we’ve always attached ourselves to. What they want when they look for partners or representation is who’s going to be able to move with us and say to our crazy ideas ‘This is possible.’ Because the talent that we work with will say, ‘Well, if it’s not you guys, then we’re going to do it ourselves. We don’t need a label, we don’t need a studio, we don’t need any of that. We have the money, we have the ingenuity, and whether or not you’re going to support us, we’re still going to build it and we’re going to win.’ ” Lee and Yan previously worked together at esports talent and marketing agencies Press X and Everyday Influencers, which were acquired by UTA in 2018. Lee and Yan then joined UTA. Yan exited UTA several years ago and was doing some consulting for Live Nation when he realized the opportunity to take popular live streamers on global tours, including in China. Yan and Lee have long-established relationships with local distribution partners that will go a long way toward helping talent make inroads in the world’s most populous country. Influence Media Partners is based in New York and specializes in developing and acquiring premium music and entertainment IP. Influence is supported by strategic partnerships with funds and accounts managed by private equity giant BlackRock. The interest in the digital native arena by one of the world’s biggest private equity firms is a sign of the times that Lee and Yan intend to capitalize on. ISO staffers gather to mark the company’s formal launch tyler ash “At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment. Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated,” said Lylette Pizarro, founder and co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.” The ISO founders see enormous opportunity ahead as the creator economy becomes more mainstream as a marketing and branding vehicle for the biggest brands (hence the interest in the arena from BlackRock). “We really have three pillars main pillars of the business: Talent driven by Mike’s team, our brand business and our music practice, which is artist management consulting,” Yan says. “With our digital native talent and with digital native advertising, we’re going to be able to bridge that gap [for marketers] and be able to drive and show more value. We were in the Twitch space 15 years ago. We’ve been fighting for experimental media budgets our entire careers,” Yan says. ISO has been established with what Lee and Yan call a policy of being “radically transparent” with their employees. The pair have developed a system of bonusing employees for success on a year-round basis, rather than doling out bonus coin once a year, with staffers receiving little information as to how the spoils were divided. The ISO founders also vow that in the effort to encourage collaboration and brainstorming among staffers, they have a formula for recognizing those contributions with bonus coin that comes out of the firm’s share of profits, not from the pool that goes to the primary representative. “The way we think about it is, every six months there is a new defecting faction out of some talent agency starting their own management company. And largely it is for very common reasons. The way we looked at it was, how do we prevent that from happening? How do we retain great talent, not just on our roster but our employees,” Lee says. “We don’t want to get to a point where we’re building this business with them, and then four or five years later they’re going to feel exactly how we felt, that we could own our own book of business and go somewhere else and make you know a lot more money that way. For us, we want to create an environment where [employees] feel like they can do that with a group of people that they trust. title: ‘Off Campus’ Gets Season 2 Release Date On Prime Video, Confirms Returning Cast
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Scrubs’ Star Sarah Chalke On J.D. & Elliot’s Big Reveal & Surprise Twist, Sean & Charlie’s Quick Exit, Ollie’s Arrival & What Comes Next ‘Red, White & Royal Blue’ Author Responds To Texas Going Blue In Midterms: “It Was All In The Binder” Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Off Campus' Prime Video Great news for Off Campus fans — the hugely popular Prime Video college soap will be back sooner than many expected, with Season 2 set to premiere on April 28, 2027. That is less than a year after the May 13 release of Season 1, a very rare gap of under 12 months for a streaming series and one of the smallest on record. Related Stories News 2026-27 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery The quick turnaround for Off Campus , created by Louisa Levy based on author Elle Kennedy’s best-selling Off Campus Universe, was helped by the early Season 2 renewal in February , three months ahead of the Season 1 debut. It is set to meet a global demand for the series which, six months after Season 1 was released, remains among Prime Video’s Top 10 most viewed series worldwide, most recently at #6 for the week of Oct. 26. Off Campus ‘ staying power followed a red-hot launch, with Season 1 reaching 36 million viewers through its first 12 days to mark the third most-viewed debut season of any series in Prime Video history overall and most-viewed ever among Women 18-34. Watch on Deadline Off Campus follows an elite ice hockey team, and the women in their lives, as they grapple with love, heartbreak, and self-discovery — forging deep friendships and enduring bonds while navigating the complexities that come with transitioning into adulthood. As announced in May , Season 2 will center on the romance between Allie Hayes (Mika Abdalla) and Dean Di Laurentis (Stephen Kalyn) from The Mistake book in Kennedy’s series. Stephen Kalyn & Mika Abdalla in ‘Off Campus’ Prime Video Along with the premiere date announcement, Amazon has confirmed the cast for Season 2. As expected, coming back is the entire Season 1 series regular cast except Josh Heuston who had a one-season arc as Hannah’s (Ella Bright) crush. Those returning include Abdalla, Kalyn, Season 1 couple Belmont Cameli (Garrett) and Bright (Hannah), as well as the other two hockey players who will get their own love stories, Antonio Cipriano (John Logan) and Jalen Thomas Brooks (John Tucker). They are joined by new series regular India Fowler who will play John Logan’s romantic interest Grace Ivers. From the Season 1 recurring cast, returning are Julia Sarah-Stone as Jules, John Logan’s younger nonbinary sibling who runs the Briar gossip account; Khobe Clarke as Beau Maxwell, Dean’s friend and brother of Joanna Maxwell; and Miles Gutierrez-Riley as Hannah’s friend Dexter. They are joined by new recurring cast member Philipa Soo as Scarlett, a theatre artist who is guest directing an original play at the college’s drama department. Guest starring in Season 2 are Charlie Evans, who was introduced late in Season 1 as Dean’s high school hockey rival Hunter Davenport, and new addition Shay Rudolph as Dean’s younger sister Summer . Among those not listed for Season 2 are Chad Willett, who played Coach Jensen, the head coach of the Briar Hawks, in Season 1; Steve Howey, who recurred as Garrett’s abusive father Phil; and Chelah Horsdal as Hannah’s mother Carrie. Levy co-showruns and executive produces Off Campus with Gina Fattore. Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen and James Seidman executive produce and Annika Patton co-executive produces for Temple Hill. Leanna Billings of Billings Productions and Neal Flaherty also serve as executive producers. title: ‘Off Campus’ Season 2 Sets April Premiere Date
full_text: Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Off Campus' season two. Prime Video Logo text Off Campus is skating back to screens this April, Prime Video announced Thursday. The popular college hockey romance series will officially return for season two on April 28, 2027. Shortly after season one premiered in May, Prime Video announced Stephen Kalyn ‘s Dean Di Laurentis and Mika Abdalla ‘s Allie Hayes would lead the next installment , which didn’t come as a big surprise to many viewers as the couple was a fan favorite in season one. Their relationship will serve as the driving force behind the new season. Season one leads, Belmont Cameli and Ella Bright , will continue to star in the series. Related Stories TV Dave Bautista Reveals He Gained 20 Pounds of Muscle for 'God of War' Series Next Big Thing Jaalen Best Wanted to Be a Pro Athlete. Now He's Playing 'The Greatest' Boxer Onscreen The new season will adapt the plot of Elle Kennedy ’s third novel in the Off Campus series, The Score . The book series Off Campus , which begins with The Deal , follows a new-but-connected couple in each book. The show plans to keep that model. Season one dove headfirst into the age-old romantic trope of fake dating with music student Hannah Wells (Bright), who, in true hockey fashion, is often called Wellsy by her love interest, Garrett Graham (Cameli). “I consider [episode six] a pilot episode or a soft launch for season two and what you’re going to expect,” Kalyn previously told The Hollywood Reporter . “I was so grateful to learn from Ella and Belmont and watch those two great phenomenal actors lead season one.” Abdalla had similar sentiments, sharing her excitement for getting to work more closely with her co-star. “I truly love working with Stephen so much,” she previously told THR ahead of the announcement she and Kalyn would lead season two. “I’m excited that I get to do this with him because I trust him so much.” Abdalla, Kalyn, Bright and Cameli are joined by Antonio Cipriano, Jalen Thomas Brooks and India Fowler as series regulars for Off Campus season two. Julia Sarah-Stone, Khobe Clarke, Miles Gutierrez-Riley and Philipa Soo are set to recur. Charlie Evans and Shay Rudolph will guest star. Off Campus has become a hit for Prime Video. title: Final Chapter Of ‘Mass Effect’ Studio BioWare To Be Told In Super Channel Feature Doc From Fennessey Films and Score G Productions
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse JioStar’s Alok Jain On Reality TV Competition, Building Indian Formats & The End Of ‘Koffee With Karan’ ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Propels Sony Pictures To Huge Q2 Profit Boost Bri Lee’s Novel ‘The Work’ Set For TV Adaptation At Dollhouse Pictures View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Massive Effect: The Bioware Story' Fennessey Films/Score G Productions EXCLUSIVE: The final days of legendary video games studio BioWare will be told in a doc from Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie for Canada ‘s Super Channel . Massive Effect: The BioWare Story will document how the Edmonton, Canada-based games company grew from being founded in 1995 by three medical doctors – Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip – to selling 100 million copies of its role-playing games, which include Mass Effect , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , Dragon Age and Baldur’s Gate . Written and directed by Akash Sherman ( Clara ) and co-produced by Canada’s Fennessey Films and Score G Productions , the film has a unique insight into the story, with filming beginning two years before Electronic Arts announced the closure of BioWare on October 21 last month and continuing to lens throughout. Related Stories News Titan1Studios Adapting Stephen R. Bown's 'The Company: The Rise and Fall Of The Hudson's Bay Empire' As Historical Drama Series News European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members This allowed the filmmakers to capture BioWare’s finale chapter, as the news of the studio’s closure reverberated through the gaming industry. EA decided to shutter studio, which was known for its complex narratives and world building, after recent releases underperformed, and 400 jobs were cut. Watch on Deadline Muzyka, Zeschuk and Yip will feature in the film, along with a plethora of major players from the video game world. These include Douglas Reilly, Vice President of Lucasfilm Games; John Riccitiello, former CEO of Electronic Arts; Casey Hudson, game director of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect ; Geoff Keighley, creator of The Game Awards; Victor Lucas, creator of The Electric Playground ; voice actor Jennifer Hale; and longtime BioWare developers Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. “When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved,” said BioWare co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk in a statement. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.” A website has also been set up for the BioWare community to share photos, videos and how the company touched their lives for the chance to appear in the film. “BioWare’s fans have been part of its journey since the very first game,” said Scorgie. “It’s only right that they help us tell the rest of the story.” “The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes,” added writer and director Sherman. “It’s a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio’s recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction.” Canada’s Super Channel commissioned the doc, which is being planned for a major film festival run and a world premiere next year. Jhod Cardinal of Upstream Flix is handling worldwide sales. The Canada Media Fund supported production. “We are thrilled to bring Massive Effect: The BioWare Story to Canadian audiences,” said Kim Ball, EVP Content & Communications for Super Channel. “As an Edmonton-based company, we’re especially proud to celebrate BioWare’s extraordinary hometown story and the people, creativity and groundbreaking storytelling behind some of the most beloved games of a generation.” Producers Fennessey Films and Score G are behind the likes of Funny Money: The Dane Cook Story , Dolph: Unbreakable , Inmate #1: The Rise of Danny Trejo , Breaking Olympia , Singhs in the Ring and The Great Ones .
